content: In adults with type 2 diabetes and advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of less than 30 mL/min, the therapeutic benefits of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are generally diminished. In such cases, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are considered the preferred treatment option. This preference is based on their ability to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia and provide cardiovascular protection.
